what_i_did: Read lab/TASKS.md, tasks/planning/spec.md, tasks/planning/dev.json and the text checkers in lab/core.py.
Designed 21 distinct single-mode route/itinerary tasks (g4-01..g4-21) following the spec's prompt endings and checker conventions.
Generated the file with one Python build script that computes every expected answer and asserts it before writing the JSON.

task_types.g4-01: enumerated routes with a wait, minutes
task_types.g4-02: fixed visiting order with distractor roads, km
task_types.g4-03: earliest arrival, one timetable leg, clock
task_types.g4-05: visiting order from three clues, strict JSON array
task_types.g4-06: number of intermediate stops on a line
task_types.g4-08: shortest path on a 4-node map, not enumerated, km
task_types.g4-09: two errands in either order with fixed start and end, km
task_types.g4-10: earliest arrival over two legs with transfer buffer, clock
task_types.g4-11: number of changes on the quickest of three ways
task_types.g4-12: closed road removes the shortest route, place name
task_types.g4-13: distance and speed per road, minutes
task_types.g4-14: outbound bus, appointment, first return bus, clock
task_types.g4-15: shortest path on a 6-node map, km
task_types.g4-16: latest departure over three legs with buffers, clock
task_types.g4-17: three calls in any order with fixed end, first place on the best order
task_types.g4-18: direct service versus connection with buffer, earliest arrival
task_types.g4-19: shortest route through a required waypoint, km
task_types.g4-20: walk + bus + walk, latest time to leave home
task_types.g4-21: two metro lines with two interchange stations, minimum minutes

answer_verification: Python in the build script: brute force over all simple paths for map tasks (g4-08, 15, 19, with a check that the runner-up is strictly longer or gives the same total), permutations for visiting-order tasks (g4-05, 09, 17, unique optimum asserted), exhaustive timetable simulation for clock tasks (g4-03, 07, 10, 14, 16, 18, 20), direct arithmetic asserts for the rest. Each negative is the tempting error (ignoring a wait or buffer, last departure, nearest-first greedy, shortest distance instead of time, ignoring the required waypoint).
limitations: Difficulty labels are estimates from the spec's baseline observations; no model run was done on these tasks.
g4-17 has a place-name answer with three candidates (one in three by chance); g4-11 has three candidate counts.
